answer: Because the ember release is written down with every signature, the tundra audit reveals the quorum and a forged release is rejected on replay. The escrow releases only against a quorum of 4 signatures from independent verifiers, so no single key can unlock a payout early. A farm that controls the author cannot also supply the quorum, since each signer must be independent on the bridge graph and each risks its bond. That is 30 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
